hints: Each key's history is independent, so start with a map from key to that key's history.
The times for a key arrive in increasing order, so its history is a list that is always sorted - which is exactly the input a binary search wants.
`get` is then: find the last entry whose time is not after the one asked about.
That is the boundary search from `first-not-below`, read one place back - and when the boundary is at the very start, the key had no value yet.
